audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads FAVOURED at 4/10 against a 45.59% win rate over 68 games, with a level chart Sion owns four of seven rows of.
audit.why: The label disagrees with both the data and the page's own chart.
audit.corrected: diff HARD, diffRating 6.5/10, Sion carry threat 6/10, and the 'Free poke forever' TL;DR replaced.

audit.why: Spikes are correctly framed: Karma's is level 1 (Mantra needs no point), Sion's are Soul Furnace at 2-3 and tank items. Level 6 correctly reads as Karma's re-stabiliser because Unstoppable Onslaught is dodgeable and she gains nothing new.

audit.whatIsWrong: Roar of the Slayer is described as shredding MR. Riot's text says it reduces Armor. Also, Decimating Smash was written as a flat knockup when only a sufficiently long charge knocks up, and Glory in Death was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Armour shred does nothing to Karma's magic damage — it sets up his damage, not hers, so the advice built on 'shreds your MR' is backwards. And a short-charge Q is a survivable slow, not a stun, which changes every step-up read.
audit.corrected: Armour stated in early, whys[3] and breakdown.cooldowns; the charge requirement in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; Glory in Death's healing max-health-damage revive written into late and report[5].
sources: kit Sion E text ('reduces the Armor'), Q text ('If he charges for enough time'), P text

audit.why: Decimating Smash 10s at rank 1 and Roar of the Slayer 12s at 800 range are the two windows that gate a 950-range poke champion.

The brief's missingInteractions listed 'terrain-cuts-retreat' for Unstoppable Onslaught, but Riot's own description of the R is a steerable charge that damages and knocks up — no terrain creation. Per the kit rules I trusted the description and did not write it.
sources: kit Sion R text vs derived terrain flag

edits.before: Your multi-Q peak gets eaten by the W shield while his Roar of the Slayer (E) slow and charged Q knockup punish every step-up.
edits.after: Your multi-Q peak gets eaten by the 15s Soul Furnace shield, while Roar of the Slayer's slow at 800 range punishes every step-up.

edits.before: Level 1 is your one clean window — Mantra is up immediately, so open with RQ Soulflare for a real chunk before his Soul Furnace (W) shield is even leveled to absorb it. The problem starts at 2-3: once W is online he times the shield to eat your Q and detonates it for AoE damage back, so your poke stops sticking on a tank. Respect his Roar of the Slayer (E) — it slows and shreds your MR to set up a charged Q knockup, so do not walk into Q range to throw a greedy poke.
edits.after: Level 1 is your one clean window — Mantra is up immediately, so open with RQ Soulflare for a real chunk before his Soul Furnace (W) shield is even leveled to absorb it. The problem starts at 2-3: once W is online he times the shield to eat your Q and detonates it for AoE damage back, so your poke stops sticking on a tank. Respect Roar of the Slayer (E) — it slows and shreds armour at 800 range to set up a charged Q knockup, so never walk into Q range for a greedy poke.

edits.before: You fall off and he comes online — two tank items and your Q barely registers on his health bar while his W shield absorbs the rest. A fully charged Q knockup or a flank R charge now locks you long enough for his team to delete your thin frame. Your only path is to have already snowballed the early tempo into roams off Gathering Fire and turned the map before his tank stats and engage make the 1v1 unwinnable; you are a utility piece here, not the win condition.
edits.after: You fall off and he comes online — two tank items and your Q barely registers while his W shield absorbs the rest. And killing him does not end him: Glory in Death reanimates Sion with rapid attacks that heal him and hit for a share of your max health, so walk away from the corpse instead of trading with it. Your only path is to have snowballed early tempo into roams off Gathering Fire before his tank stats make the 1v1 unwinnable; you are a utility piece, not the win condition.

edits.before: - Sion Decimating Smash (Stun): matchup-defining — Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sion Decimating Smash: 10s at rank 1, and only a fully charged swing knocks up — a short charge is damage and a slow, nothing more. - Roar of the Slayer is 12s at 800 range: it shreds armour, not MR, so it sets up his damage, never yours.

edits.before: Track Sion’s Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Decimating Smash only knocks up on a full charge — a short one is just damage and slow. Glory in Death revives him; walk away, don't trade.

notes: The MR/armour error mattered: Roar of the Slayer reduces Armor, so it amplifies his damage and does nothing to Karma's magic damage — the page had the player fearing the wrong consequence. Level chart already agreed across both layers and with the packet, so no chart edits. I did NOT write the brief's 'terrain-cuts-retreat' interaction: the derived terrain flag on Unstoppable Onslaught contradicts Riot's description, which is a steerable charge with a knockup and no wall.
